openItems.explanation: Invoice HGC-26-1043 (Pier 9 Tech Center, 166 office suites) charged 10.30% for Bellevue (1704), but the job site is Seattle (1726) at 10.55%. The return reports the job-site rate: $113,600.00 x 10.55% = $11,984.80, against $11,700.80 charged. $284.00 was not collected from the owner. A person decides whether to rebill; no plug posted.

No reseller permit on file from Summit Line Construction Co. for invoice HGC-26-1048 ($240,000.00). The job list shows the first billing on October 30, 2026, so the permit can still be obtained by February 27, 2027 (120 days, WAC 458-20-102). The draft keeps it in wholesaling. Until the permit arrives a person decides; if it never arrives, retail sales tax of $25,320.00 would be due. No plug posted.

The October trial balance is unapproved. The client's email of 02 Nov 2026 says it has not been approved yet. The draft uses the supplied general ledger and registers; its figures change only when an approved export is supplied.

This is an unsigned draft in the return's sections, not the Department's form. A person reviews it, decides the open items and the retail treatment of Juniper Ridge Partners, 9 flex units, with no reseller permit or exemption certificate on file, and files and pays in My DOR by November 25, 2026. Nothing has been filed or paid.

rules.question: When is the October 2026 monthly return due, and when do late penalties begin?
rules.whyItMatters: Sets the filing and payment deadline and the dates the 9%, 19% and 29% late payment penalties start.
rules.effective: The Department's 2026 due date table for monthly filers.
rules.excerpt: October 2026 Return due date: 11/25/26 9% penalty begins: 11/26/26 19% penalty begins: 01/01/27 29% penalty begins: 02/02/27
matchPhrases: October 2026 Return due date: 11/25/26 9% penalty begins: 11/26/26 19% penalty begins: 01/01/27 29% penalty begins: 02/02/27
the due date is extended to the next business day
rules.ruleOrLimit: The October 2026 monthly return is due 11/25/26. A 9% penalty begins 11/26/26, 19% on 01/01/27 and 29% on 02/02/27. A due date on a weekend or legal holiday moves to the next business day.
rules.hangsApplication: HANGS Construction Services files monthly, so this draft for October 2026 is due Wednesday, November 25, 2026, and the stated date needs no weekend move. The draft shows $780,041.68 due. As of November 5, 2026 the date has not passed. Paying after November 25 would add a 9% penalty, $70,203.75 on that amount, rising to 19% on January 1, 2027 and 29% on February 2, 2027.
rules.unresolved: Nothing on the date. A person files and pays in My DOR.

rules.question: Is a monthly return the right frequency for this business?
rules.whyItMatters: The frequency the Department assigned decides which period this return covers.
rules.effective: The Department's filing frequency page, retrieved for this run.
rules.excerpt: Monthly returns are due the 25th of every month. (e.g. the June tax return is due July 25.)
matchPhrases: monthly returns are due the 25th of every month
monthly annual tax liability $4,801 - greater
rules.pageOrSection: Filing frequencies based on annual tax liability; Due dates
rules.ruleOrLimit: The Department assigns the frequency; businesses with annual tax liability of $4,801 or more are generally monthly. Monthly returns are due the 25th of the following month.
rules.hangsApplication: The entity information states the account is assigned a monthly frequency. October alone shows $780,041.68 of tax, far above $4,801 a year, so monthly is consistent with the Department's table. The return covers October 1 to October 31, 2026 only.
rules.unresolved: The assigned frequency is the client's statement; the Department's welcome letter was not supplied.

rules.question: What B&O rates apply to retailing and wholesaling?
rules.whyItMatters: Every dollar of contract revenue is taxed under one of these two classifications on this return.
rules.effective: The Department's current classification table, retrieved for this run.
matchPhrases: retailing .00471
wholesaling .00484
rules.ruleOrLimit: Retailing is taxed at .00471 (0.471%) and wholesaling at .00484 (0.484%) of gross income.
rules.hangsApplication: Retailing gross $7,030,000.00 x 0.471% = $33,111.30. Wholesaling gross $852,500.00 x 0.484% = $4,126.10. B&O total $37,237.40. The client's rate table carries the same two rates.
rules.unresolved: No B&O credits or deductions were researched or claimed; a person confirms none apply.

rules.question: Which classification does each job's billing belong to?
rules.whyItMatters: Prime contract billings are retailing and carry retail sales tax; subcontract billings are wholesaling and carry none, if documented.
rules.effective: The Department's construction industry guide, retrieved for this run.
rules.excerpt: The income from custom prime contracting (without deduction for any amounts paid to subcontractors) is reported under the retailing B&O tax classification and is subject to retail sales tax unless a specific exemption applies.
matchPhrases: the income from custom prime contracting (without deduction for any amounts paid to subcontractors) is reported under the retailing b&o tax classification and is subject to retail sales tax
income from custom subcontracting is reported under the wholesaling b&o tax classification
subcontractors on custom construction projects (a wholesaling activity) must obtain a reseller permit from the prime contractor or another subcontractor
rules.pageOrSection: Construction categories for tax purposes; Custom construction
rules.ruleOrLimit: Custom prime contracting is retailing and subject to retail sales tax, without deduction for amounts paid to subcontractors. Custom subcontracting is wholesaling, and the subcontractor must obtain a reseller permit from the prime contractor.
rules.hangsApplication: Five jobs are prime contracts for the landowner (J-2611, J-2604, J-2617, J-2622, J-2625): $7,030,000.00 retailing. Two jobs are subcontracts for other prime contractors (J-2619 for Cedar Ridge Builders, J-2627 for Summit Line Construction): $852,500.00 wholesaling. Cedar Ridge's permit RP-0418-2207 is on file; Summit Line's is not (see reseller-permit-120-days).
rules.unresolved: The wholesale treatment of HGC-26-1048 depends on a permit not yet received.

rules.question: What is the measure of B&O and retail sales tax on a construction contract?
rules.whyItMatters: Decides whether costs, subcontractor charges or retainage may be taken out of the amount taxed.
rules.effective: WAC 458-20-170 as published; the page states no agency filings affecting the section since 2003.
rules.excerpt: (a) Prime contractors are taxable under the retailing classification, and subcontractors under the wholesaling classification upon the gross contract price. ... (a) Prime contractors are required to collect from consumers the retail sales tax measured by the full contract price.
matchPhrases: prime contractors are taxable under the retailing classification, and subcontractors under the wholesaling classification upon the gross contract price
prime contractors are required to collect from consumers the retail sales tax measured by the full contract price
rules.ruleOrLimit: B&O is measured by the gross contract price; retail sales tax by the full contract price.
rules.hangsApplication: The B&O and retail sales tax lines use the full October billings: $7,030,000.00 retail and $852,500.00 subcontract, with nothing deducted for subcontractor costs or materials.
hangsFactsUsed: October billing register, billed this period
rules.sourceTitle: WAC 458-20-170, Constructing and repairing of new or existing buildings or other structures upon real property

rules.question: Is retainage held by the owner deducted before B&O and sales tax?
rules.whyItMatters: Every October invoice holds back 5%; deducting it would understate the return.
rules.effective: The Department's custom construction guide, retrieved for this run.
rules.excerpt: If the contract requires retainage, sales tax must be computed before deducting such amounts. ... On the excise tax return, report the full selling price without a deduction for retainage under the Retailing B&O tax classification and retail sales tax.
matchPhrases: if the contract requires retainage, sales tax must be computed before deducting such amounts
report the full selling price without a deduction for retainage under the retailing b&o tax classification and retail sales tax
rules.ruleOrLimit: Sales tax is computed before retainage is deducted, and the return reports the full selling price without a deduction for retainage.
rules.hangsApplication: Retail invoices hold back $351,500.00 of retainage in October, and subcontract invoices $42,625.00. None of it is deducted: retailing and retail sales tax are reported on $7,030,000.00, and wholesaling on $852,500.00.
hangsFactsUsed: Retainage held column of the October billing register

rules.question: Is the Juniper Ridge work for Juniper Ridge Partners LLC, with no reseller permit or exemption certificate on file, a retail sale?
rules.whyItMatters: Decides whether $618,000.00 of October billing is retailing with sales tax, or wholesaling without it.
rules.excerpt: (a) The term "prime contractor" means a person engaged in the business of performing for consumers, the constructing, repairing, decorating or improving of new or existing buildings or other structures under, upon or above real property ... (b) The word "subcontractor" means a person engaged in the business of performing a similar service for persons other than consumers.
matchPhrases: means a person engaged in the business of performing for consumers
constructing, repairing, decorating or improving of new or existing buildings or other structures under, upon or above real property
means a person engaged in the business of performing a similar service for persons other than consumers
rules.ruleOrLimit: A prime contractor builds for consumers and makes retail sales. Work for a person who is not the consumer, such as a buyer for resale, is a subcontract; without a reseller permit or exemption certificate from the customer, the work is a retail sale.
rules.hangsApplication: Invoice HGC-26-1046 bills $618,000.00 to Juniper Ridge Partners LLC for its Juniper Ridge flex industrial units, Seattle. The draft treats HANGS Construction Services as a prime contractor making a retail sale: retailing B&O and Seattle sales tax at 10.55%, $65,199.00, are included. No reseller permit or exemption certificate from Juniper Ridge Partners LLC is on file.
rules.unresolved: Reason: no reseller permit or exemption certificate from Juniper Ridge Partners LLC is on file, and no supplied document shows how it will use the units. A person confirms the retail treatment before filing.
rules.sourceTitle: WAC 458-20-170, Constructing and repairing of new or existing buildings or other structures upon real property

rules.question: Can HGC-26-1048 to Summit Line Construction be reported as wholesale without a reseller permit on file?
rules.whyItMatters: Without the permit, the $240,000.00 billing would be a retail sale with Seattle sales tax.
rules.effective: WAC 458-20-102 as published, retrieved for this run.
rules.excerpt: A subcontractor entering into a construction contract for which it has not received a reseller permit must obtain it within one hundred twenty days of the initial construction draw request.
matchPhrases: the seller may obtain a reseller permit within one hundred twenty days after the first billing
a subcontractor entering into a construction contract for which it has not received a reseller permit must obtain it within one hundred twenty days of the initial construction draw request
rules.ruleOrLimit: A seller without a reseller permit at the time of sale may obtain one within 120 days after the first billing; a construction subcontractor must obtain it within 120 days of the initial draw request.
rules.hangsApplication: Only Cedar Ridge Builders' permit RP-0418-2207 is on file. HGC-26-1048, $240,000.00 billed October 30, 2026 for Lakeside Clinic, has none. The job list shows October 30, 2026 as the first billing, so the permit can still be obtained by February 27, 2027. The draft keeps it in wholesaling; if the permit never arrives, Seattle sales tax at 10.55%, $25,320.00, would be due.
hangsFactsUsed: Job list first billing for J-2627
rules.unresolved: Summit Line Construction Co.'s reseller permit is missing (RESALE-01). No plug is posted.

rules.question: Which location code and rate apply to retail construction billings?
rules.whyItMatters: Local sales tax is reported by location code; the wrong code moves tax between cities and changes the rate.
rules.effective: The Department's custom construction guide, retrieved for this run.
rules.excerpt: Retail construction services are sourced to the location where the construction takes place. This means construction that takes place in Seattle is sourced to Seattle (location code 1726) and taxed at Seattle's combined state and local sales tax rate.
matchPhrases: retail construction services are sourced to the location where the construction takes place
construction that takes place in seattle is sourced to seattle (location code 1726)
rules.pageOrSection: Collecting sales tax - local tax rates
rules.ruleOrLimit: Retail construction is sourced to the job site, whatever address the owner or the invoice shows.
rules.hangsApplication: The draft reports each retail billing at its job site from the job list: Bellevue 1704 $2,180,000.00, Seattle 1726 $3,540,000.00, Tacoma 2717 $1,310,000.00. Change order 7 on Pier 9 Tech Center (HGC-26-1043, $113,600.00) is a Seattle site billed at Bellevue's rate, so it is reported under 1726.
hangsFactsUsed: October billing register tax location codes
rules.unresolved: Nothing on sourcing. Whether to rebill the owner is miscoded-invoice-rebill.

rules.question: HGC-26-1043 charged the owner Bellevue's 10.30% instead of Seattle's 10.55%. Should the owner be rebilled?
rules.whyItMatters: The return owes tax at the job-site rate either way; the $284.00 under-collected is either rebilled or absorbed.
rules.effective: The Department's custom construction guide, retrieved for this run.
rules.excerpt: Billing invoices must separately state the sales tax. ... Progress billings made against the total contract price of a job should separately state the sales tax.
matchPhrases: billing invoices must separately state the sales tax
progress billings made against the total contract price of a job should separately state the sales tax
rules.pageOrSection: Collecting retail sales tax; Bid, contract, pay estimate, or draw request
rules.ruleOrLimit: Sales tax must be separately stated on billings. The tax owed follows the job site, not the rate printed on the invoice.
rules.hangsApplication: Invoices charged $735,276.00 of sales tax; tax at job-site rates is $735,560.00. The $284.00 difference is HGC-26-1043: $113,600.00 at 10.55% is $11,984.80, but the invoice states $11,700.80. The draft reports the job-site amount and shows the $284.00 as an open difference, not plugged.
rules.unresolved: Whether to issue a corrected invoice to Pier Nine Commercial LLC for $284.00 is a business decision for a person (LOC-01).

rules.question: What are the Q4 2026 local and combined rates for Bellevue, Seattle and Tacoma?
rules.whyItMatters: October falls in Q4 2026; the local tax and use tax lines use these rates.
rules.effective: Effective October 1 - December 31, 2026, as printed on the flyer.
matchPhrases: effective october 1 - december 31, 2026
rules.pageOrSection: Quarter 4 2026 Local Sales and Use Tax Rates, King and Pierce counties
rules.ruleOrLimit: Bellevue 1704: local .0380, combined .1030. Seattle 1726: local .0405, combined .1055. Tacoma 2717: local .0400, combined .1050. State rate .0650.

Local use tax: Seattle $64,800.00 x 4.05% = $2,624.40; Bellevue $3,960.00 x 3.80% = $150.48. The client's rate table matches the flyer.

rules.question: What goes on the state retail sales tax line?
rules.whyItMatters: The retail sales gross must agree with the retailing B&O gross, and the state rate is printed on the return.
rules.effective: The Department's return instructions, retrieved for this run.
rules.excerpt: This amount must be the same as the gross amount for retailing in your business and occupation tax section. ... Multiply the taxable amount by the tax rate shown (0.065) and write this amount in tax due.
matchPhrases: this amount must be the same as the gross amount for retailing in your business and occupation tax section
multiply the taxable amount by the tax rate shown (0.065)
rules.ruleOrLimit: Retail sales gross equals the retailing B&O gross; state tax is the taxable amount times 0.065.
rules.hangsApplication: Retail sales gross $7,030,000.00 equals retailing gross. No deductions are claimed. State sales tax $7,030,000.00 x 6.5% = $456,950.00.
rules.sourceTitle: Combined Excise Tax Return: State Sales and Use Tax

rules.question: Which October purchases owe use tax?
rules.whyItMatters: Tools, equipment and supplies a contractor uses without paying Washington sales tax are taxed on the return.
rules.effective: The Department's return instructions, retrieved for this run.
rules.excerpt: Use tax applies to the value of all articles you used in your business (as opposed to being sold to a customer) on which no Washington sales tax has been paid.
matchPhrases: use tax applies to the value of all articles you used in your business (as opposed to being sold to a customer) on which no washington sales tax has been paid
multiply the value of articles by the rate shown (0.065)
rules.ruleOrLimit: Use tax applies to articles used in the business on which no Washington sales tax was paid; the state rate is 0.065.
rules.hangsApplication: Two purchases qualify: the Idaho track loader AP-7741, $64,800.00, and the online safety harnesses AP-7752, $3,960.00. Value of articles $68,760.00 x 6.5% = $4,469.40. The Oregon rebar AP-7730, $86,400.00, became part of Pier 9 Tech Center, a retail job, so it is a purchase for resale. The formwork plywood AP-7758 was charged $1,278.66 of Washington sales tax, so no use tax is due.
rules.unresolved: Only the purchases register was reviewed for use tax; other October purchases were not.
rules.sourceTitle: Combined Excise Tax Return: State Sales and Use Tax

rules.question: Which local rate applies to use tax, and in which period is it reported?
rules.whyItMatters: Local use tax follows the place of first use, not the vendor's address.
rules.effective: The Department's use tax page, retrieved for this run.
rules.excerpt: The use tax rate is determined by the location in Washington where the consumer (purchaser) first uses the items purchased. Use tax is made of the state rate (6.5%) plus the local use tax rate.
matchPhrases: the use tax rate is determined by the location in washington where the consumer (purchaser) first uses the items purchased
use tax is made of the state rate (6.5%) plus the local use tax rate
the use tax must be reported in the period when the goods are first used in the state
rules.pageOrSection: How do you determine the correct use tax rate? How do I pay use tax?
rules.ruleOrLimit: Use tax is the state 6.5% plus the local rate where the item is first used, reported in the period of first use.
rules.hangsApplication: The track loader was first used in Seattle (1726) in October: $64,800.00 x 10.55% = $6,836.40. The harnesses were first used in Bellevue (1704) in October: $3,960.00 x 10.30% = $407.88. Use tax total $7,244.28.
hangsFactsUsed: Purchases register location first used and dates
rules.unresolved: First-use location and month are the client's statements in the purchases register.

rules.question: How are local sales and use taxes entered, and what must they agree with?
rules.whyItMatters: The local section must foot to the state section or the Department will question the return.
rules.effective: The Department's return instructions, retrieved for this run.
rules.excerpt: Write the location codes and rates in the appropriate columns for each location where retail sales took place. ... This amount must be the same as your taxable amount for retail sales in column 3.
matchPhrases: write the location codes and rates in the appropriate columns for each location where retail sales took place
this amount must be the same as your taxable amount for retail sales in column 3
this amount must be the same as your taxable amount for use tax/deferred sales tax in column 1
rules.pageOrSection: Local sales tax; Local use tax/deferred sales tax
rules.ruleOrLimit: Local taxable amounts are listed by location code; their total must equal the state retail sales taxable amount, and the local use values must total the state use tax value.
rules.hangsApplication: Local taxable amounts 1704, 1726 and 2717 total $7,030,000.00, equal to the state retail sales taxable amount. Local use values 1704 and 1726 total $68,760.00, equal to the state use tax value. Local sales tax $278,610.00; local use tax $2,774.88.
